beliefs.practice: Read the cluster connection string only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime; never hard-code or log the full connection string or credentials in source, logs, or checked-in files.

Create the Mongo/PyMongo client with explicit connection-tuning options: set a reasonable maxPoolSize (e.g. 50), minPoolSize (e.g. 0–1), serverSelectionTimeoutMS (e.g. 5000) and socketTimeoutMS to avoid long blocking on network failures.
Use TLS/SSL for all connections (ensure the connection string enforces ssl=true / tls=true and validate the server certificate) and do not disable certificate verification in production.
Make seeding idempotent: perform upserts or conditional inserts (e.g., insertMany with ordered=false and handle duplicate-key errors), so re-running seed scripts does not create duplicate documents.

Index pattern for the wallet analytics workload: create a compound index { wallet_address: 1, timestamp: 1 } (or timestamp: -1 for recent-first reads) so equality on wallet_address plus range scans by timestamp are covered.

When grouping by day in the server aggregation, either store a pre-computed 'date_bucket' (YYYY-MM-DD) field at write time, or use a date-trunc operator (e.g. $dateTrunc) early in the pipeline so grouping keys are efficient and deterministic.

Structure aggregation pipelines to $match by wallet_address and time-range as the first stages so the query can use the {wallet_address, timestamp} index and reduce scanned documents before $group and heavy computation.

Use explain() (or the provider's aggregation explain) on representative aggregation pipelines to verify the index is being used and to measure examined vs returned documents; adjust indexes or pipeline order if explain shows collection scan.

For heavy aggregations, enable allowDiskUse=True on the aggregation cursor so large group/sort operations do not fail due to memory limits; additionally consider batching time ranges or summarizing at ingest to avoid large working sets.

Compute statistical metrics (daily sum, count, mean, stdDev) inside a server-side aggregation where possible (use $group, $avg, $stdDevSamp or two-pass pipelines) to reduce network transfer and to produce exact aggregates on the server.

When implementing z-score outlier detection in aggregation, compute mean and stdDev for the matched time window in one sub-pipeline, then join back to per-day buckets for a single-pass logical result instead of pulling raw rows into client memory.

Project only required fields (use projection in find/aggregate $project) to minimize network payload; when aggregating by day only require wallet_address, timestamp, and amount (omit large or unneeded fields).
Handle transient errors with exponential backoff and jitter for retries (network timeouts, failovers, 429/TooManyRequests); make read/aggregation operations idempotent so retries are safe.

Tune provisioning/throughput for the collection: for Azure Cosmos-style clusters provision RU/s or autoscale appropriate for expected aggregate queries and writes; avoid surprise 429s by estimating RU cost of the aggregation and increasing throughput or splitting queries.

For interactive analysis, include time-range pagination and server-side limits ($limit) so the analyzer can run within acceptable RU and latency bounds instead of scanning multi-year wallets in one query.

Record and expose query metrics and logs: capture aggregation explain metrics, query durations, documentsExamined/documentsReturned and 429s so you can tune indexes and throughput from observed behavior.

If you plan to use vector search features: store dense float vectors in a dedicated field, create the provider-specific vector index (HNSW/IVF) with explicit parameters (space metric, efConstruction, M, efSearch) and pin vector dimension and metric in schema; run approximate search server-side to avoid moving large vector sets over the network.

Apply least-privilege credentials for the account used by the sample (limit to the sample_fintech_09 db and collections) and rotate credentials regularly; use managed identity or Key Vault where available to avoid long-lived secrets in env files.

Use server-side summarization or optional LLM call only after local rule-based summarization fallback: ensure the pipeline returns a compact summary payload to the summarizer (not the full raw transaction list), and guard LLM calls with token/length limits and API key checks.

When creating indexes, create them with explicit names and background/async creation where supported, and ensure index creation is idempotent in deployment scripts (check existence before create) to avoid production downtime during index builds.
